topic: Head and neck cancer two-week-wait pathway

audits.title: 1648 Is Telephone Triage Here to Stay? An Audit of The Impact of COVID 19 On A Head and Neck Cancer Clinic
audits.setting: Head and neck cancer clinic, district general hospital (Wirral University Teaching Hospital)

cycle1.result: 96.9% seen within 14 days; 98.7% initially reviewed by telephone; for cancer patients, telephone vs face-to-face: 80% v 57% diagnosed by 28 days and 100% v 17% started treatment by 62 days.

audits.other_findings: Referrals dropped 1.4% compared with 2019; 11.2% diagnosed with cancer.
audits.citation: Osuji J, Srinivasan V. 1648 Is Telephone Triage Here to Stay? An Audit of The Impact of COVID 19 On A Head and Neck Cancer Clinic. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.578.

audits.title: An audit of the UK national cancer referral guidelines for suspected oral mucosal malignancy.
audits.standard: UK National Cancer Referral Guidelines for suspected oral mucosal malignancy (2000)
audits.setting: Oral medicine unit, Eastman Dental Hospital, London (university teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 487 of 901 referrals classed as potentially malignant; in a subgroup of 241, 18 had malignant (8) or dysplastic (10) lesions; guidelines missed 15% of malignant or dysplastic lesions.

audits.other_findings: Only 9 of 75 persistent ulcer referrals and 8 of 116 white patch referrals were malignant or dysplastic; missed lesions presented with orofacial pain of unknown cause.
audits.citation: Hodgson TA, Buchanan JA, Garg A, Ilyas SE, Porter SR. An audit of the UK national cancer referral guidelines for suspected oral mucosal malignancy. Br Dent J. 2006;201(10):643-647. doi:10.1038/sj.bdj.4814262. PMID: 17128234.

audits.title: Do GP referral guidelines really work? Audit of an electronic urgent referral system for suspected head and neck cancer.
audits.standard: 2002 Scottish Referral Guidelines for suspected head and neck cancer (alarm symptoms)
audits.setting: Electronic SeCURE urgent referral system, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Overall poor compliance with referral guidelines; 15 of 190 (8%) diagnosed with SCCHN.

audits.other_findings: Electronic referral gave speedy appointments; steps taken to reinforce GP awareness.
audits.citation: Kennedy AM, Aziz A, Khalid S, Hurman D. Do GP referral guidelines really work? Audit of an electronic urgent referral system for suspected head and neck cancer. Eur Arch Otorhinolaryngol. 2012;269(5):1509-1512. doi:10.1007/s00405-011-1788-3. PMID: 21984061.

audits.title: A multidisciplinary audit of head and neck referrals: considerations for patients' timelines and outcomes.
audits.standard: NICE 2004 Improving outcomes in head and neck cancer; 2-week wait referrals
audits.setting: Head and neck clinic, Barts Health, London

cycle1.result: Mean time from referral to being seen 11 days for 2-week wait referrals and 34 days for other referrals.

audits.intervention: One-stop Rapid Diagnostic Clinic with on-site ultrasound and cytology.

cycle2.result: Mean waiting time 9 days for 2-week wait and 23 days for other referrals; most reached a definitive outcome at first consultation.

audits.other_findings: Over one-third used ultrasound with or without FNAC during the RDC period.
audits.citation: Choudhury N, Hassen Y, Siddiqui J, Falzon A, Ghufoor K. A multidisciplinary audit of head and neck referrals: considerations for patients' timelines and outcomes. Eur Arch Otorhinolaryngol. 2013;270(12):3121-3126. doi:10.1007/s00405-013-2453-9. PMID: 23536138.

audits.title: Cutting cancer waiting times: streamlining cervical lymph node biopsy.
audits.standard: National cancer services guidelines for waiting times

cycle1.result: Guidelines not met; median wait from referral to biopsy 74 days (IQR 47-113).

audits.intervention: Referral proforma and a co-ordinator arranging biopsy appointments.
audits.citation: Dimbleby G, Golding L, Al Hamarneh O, Ahmad I. Cutting cancer waiting times: streamlining cervical lymph node biopsy. J Laryngol Otol. 2013;127(10):1007-1011. doi:10.1017/s0022215113002004. PMID: 24074011.

audits.title: An audit to analyse the two-week wait pathway at an oral cancer specialist district general hospital.
audits.standard: Two-week wait (14 days); diagnosis within 28 days of referral; treatment within 62 days
audits.setting: Oral cancer specialist district general hospital (North Manchester General Hospital)

cycle1.result: Malignancy yield 7.38%; 19 patients breached 14 days; 45.2% of positive patients diagnosed after 28 days and 22.2% treated after 62 days

audits.other_findings: An earlier first cycle analysed one month of referrals but was too small to make recommendations.
audits.citation: Araghi AS, Harris Y, Kyzas P. An audit to analyse the two-week wait pathway at an oral cancer specialist district general hospital. Br Dent J. 2020;228(9):693-699. doi:10.1038/s41415-020-1449-2. PMID: 32385464.

audits.title: Compliance and Effectiveness of the Scottish Referral Guidelines for Suspected Head and Neck Cancer: A Comparative Audit of 7088 Referrals.
audits.standard: Scottish Referral Guidelines for Suspected Cancer (2019)
audits.setting: ENT department, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde

cycle1.result: Compliance with 2014 guidance 55.1%; all-cancer detection rate 11.6% (8.6% primary head and neck cancer).

cycle2.result: Compliance 72.5% in referral letters but 48.9% on clinic assessment; all-cancer detection 8.6% (6.2% primary head and neck cancer).

audits.other_findings: Referrals increased by 110%; 7088 referrals in total; baseline data from a previous study.
audits.citation: Denton OG, Morrison R, Zahra B, Drake I, Montgomery J. Compliance and Effectiveness of the Scottish Referral Guidelines for Suspected Head and Neck Cancer: A Comparative Audit of 7088 Referrals. Clin Otolaryngol. 2026;51(5):694-699. doi:10.1111/coa.70122. PMID: 42171364.
